hypotheses.hypothesis: FRANK effect safety requires four semantically distinct stages: cognition consistency, effect-time freshness, execution authority, and outcome certainty/recoverability.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Fresh revalidation plus valid capability authority is sufficient; outcome recovery needs no first-class semantic state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Crash/retry experiments across all supported external adapters show that fresh revalidation plus valid authority always reconstructs the truthful outcome without duplication, loss, or ambiguous retry decisions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stable effect_operation_id bound to a semantic request fingerprint is required for generic retry/reconciliation across FRANK runtime restart boundaries.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Runtime-local trace sequence plus adapter arguments are sufficient identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: A simpler identity scheme survives post-apply/pre-receipt crash, retry, semantic payload drift, duplicate delivery, stale replay and concurrent recovery without false dedupe or duplicate effect.

hypotheses.hypothesis: UNCERTAIN must be a first-class effect outcome when a non-idempotent/non-queryable external sink cannot be reconciled after an ambiguous crash.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Every ambiguous case can safely collapse to RETRY or FAILED.
hypotheses.falsifier: For every production adapter class, a deterministic retry/failed policy can be shown to avoid both duplicates and lost effects under all preregistered crash windows.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current implementation candidates need an executable negative-result lineage gate so still-applicable historical falsifiers cannot disappear during candidate replacement.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Conventional current-component tests and review provide equivalent protection at lower cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Seeded-regression trials show ordinary tests detect the same relevant semantic regressions with equal or lower false-pass rate, detection latency and maintenance cost than explicit lineage closure.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Effect-relevant dependency revalidation can preserve freshness with fewer false aborts than invalidating every proposal on any global epoch change.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Dependency discovery cost/omission risk outweighs false-abort savings; global epoch invalidation is safer and cheaper overall.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target traces show relevant-closure bookkeeping plus omission-induced stale actions has worse utility/safety/cost than global epoch invalidation at matched workload.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A bounded evidence-preserving ActiveAssembly with conflict/provenance controls and re-expansion yields better local-4B task utility per token/KV/latency cost than broad retrieval, full-context forcing or naive summaries.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The assembly compiler discards useful evidence and spends budget on bookkeeping; simpler retrieval is superior.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched local-4B trials show no utility/correction advantage or a dominated cost-quality Pareto frontier across representative tasks and OOD/conflict regimes.

hypotheses.hypothesis: FRANK should expose heterogeneous typed loop trajectories and evaluate halting with controller-independent/post-hoc baselines before selecting an adaptive recurrence controller.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A single learned or heuristic recurrence controller is sufficient and post-hoc/fixed-prior baselines add little information.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched recurrence experiments show controller conclusions and task outcomes are invariant to trajectory/readout decoupling across difficulty, noise, stalls and overthinking regimes.

hypotheses.hypothesis: At the current checkpoint, Needle should remain staged as no-tool necessity gate -> tool-positive retrieval -> proposal -> structural validation -> authority, rather than treating the contrastive retrieval head as a unified selector.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A retrained unified selector with explicit no-tool representation can dominate the staged design at matched cost and calibration.
hypotheses.falsifier: A unified selector demonstrates superior calibrated no-tool/tool selection, correct tool/args routing and OOD behavior without erasing authority separation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Timing-sensitive FRANK causal tests must bind observer/probe configuration into execution identity until paired-trajectory noninterference is demonstrated.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Logical read-only instrumentation is sufficiently noninterfering for causal comparisons.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched target-host no/disabled/armed/sampled/inline probe modes show preregistered equivalence in paired ordering, semantic outcomes and emergence readouts near timing margins.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The final one-binary H3 can physically collapse services only if snapshot, freshness, authority, operation identity, outcome uncertainty and reconciliation remain non-bypassable semantic distinctions.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Physical consolidation can safely merge some of these stages without explicit semantic identities.
hypotheses.falsifier: H3 differential tests show merged semantics preserve H1/H2 interventions, crash recovery, stale-state rejection and authority invariants with no observational or causal divergence.

required_null: Conventional persistent event-driven local architecture with bounded retrieval, explicit typed state/versioning, deterministic capability gateway, ordinary retry/reconciliation patterns and no claim of GWT/emergence advantage.
